R. Sahu, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal Order on Board 10.12.2024 1.

This appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, challenging the award dated 15.06.2016 passed by 6th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Durg (C.G.) in Claim Case No.153/2014, whereby the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.32,70,000/- with interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, in favour of the claimants for their irreparable loss.
2.

entities.text: 6th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Durg (C.G.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The facts, necessary for disposal of the present appeal, in brief, are that on 11.03.2014 at about 8:30 a.m., deceased Sanjay Malvi along with his friend Amit Patley was going from Kharkhatola Dongargarh to Bortalaw on the motorcycle.

When they reached near village Kharkhatola,
respondent no.5 Vishwadas Deshmukh driving the offending vehicle i.e. Tata Sumo Spacio MH 41 C 0179 in a rash and negligent manner dashed their motorcycle, as a result of which, Sanjay Malvi suffered grievous injuries and died on the spot whereas Amit Patley got seriously injured.

Upon report being made in this regard, crime was registered against driver Vishwadas Deshmukh at PS Dongargarh, District Rajnandgaon (CG).
3.
It was claimed that at the time of accident, deceased Sanjay Malvi was aged about 42 years and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by working as a Supervisor under Amar Builders, Durg.
Due to the casual death of deceased Sanjay Malvi, there is an irreparable loss to the claimants who are the wife, children and father of the deceased.
Therefore, the claimants preferred an application before the Claims Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs.33,46,000/-.
4. Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents brought on record, assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per month i.e. Rs.1,80,000/- per annum.
The Tribunal added 50% of the income towards future prospects and after addition, the amount came to Rs.2,70,000.
Since there were 4 claimants, 1/4th of the income was deducted towards personal expenses and after deduction, the amount came to Rs.2,02,500/-.

Considering the age of deceased to be 42 years,
multiplier of 14 was applied and the total loss of dependency worked out to Rs.28,35,000/-.
In addition, a total amount of Rs.4,35,000/- has been awarded under other heads.

Accordingly, the Claims Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.32,70,000/- in favour of the claimants with interest @ 9% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, against which the present The Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs Smt. Sarita Malvi on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142830798/
2 appeal has been filed by the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for appellant Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal has failed to appreciate the aspect of contributory negligence as the deceased driving the motorcycle rashly and negligently dashed the Tata Sumo which was being driven slowly by respondent no.5.
He submits that the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is on higher side.
He further submits that the Tribunal has erred in awarded 50% of the income towards future prospects whereas considering the age of the deceased it should have been 30%.
The amount awarded under other heads is also excessive.
Hence, excessive compensation has been awarded by the Tribunal which needs to be reduced suitably.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondents submit that the impugned award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not require any interference.
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8. As regards contributory negligence, no evidence has been presented by the appellant insurance company in support of its argument that there was any contributing negligence in the accident.
The Insurance Company has cited the statement of the driver of the offending vehicle, Vishwasdas Deshmukh.
According to which, he was driving the offending vehicle slowly and the motorcyclist came and collided with it.

It is noteworthy that this witness Vishwasdas Deshmukh has accepted in cross-examination that due to his negligence in the accident, the offending vehicle was seized and a criminal case has been registered against him by the Police.
He had not made any complaint against the driver of the motorcyclist anywhere.

It is noteworthy that in the case, Amit Patley, who was travelling on the motorcycle along with the deceased at the time of accident has been examined by the claimant side, has also said that the accident occurred due to rash & negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, which is also confirmed by the documents of the charge sheet and could not be refuted.
In such a situation, the argument of the appellant insurance company that there was any contributory negligence on the part of the deceased in the case is not acceptable.
Therefore, the first argument of the insurance company is rejected.

9. The second argument of the insurance company is that the income of the deceased has been assessed higher, the percentage of future prospects given by the Tribunal is more and the amount awarded under other heads is also excessive.

10. If we consider the question of deceased Sanjay Malvi's income, it is clear from the claimants'
evidence that he was working as a supervisor at M/s Amar Infrastructure Limited and his monthly income has been assessed as Rs.15,000/-.
This has been confirmed by Amit Kumar Patley, who worked with the deceased and Jai Prakash Sen, who worked as an office-in-charge under that Builder.
The First Information Report (Exhibit P-2) also confirms that deceased Sanjay Malvi was working as a supervisor at Amar Infrastructure at the time of the accident.

From the oral statements of the claimants' witnesses, the salary certificate (Exhibit P-12) presented by them, the authorizing letter of Jai Prakash Sen (Exhibit P-13) for evidence and the computer ledger report attached with it,
it has been established that the monthly income of the deceased Sanjay Malvi was Rs.15,000/-,

3 which could not be refuted in any way.

sentences.text: Therefore, the argument of the insurance company that the monthly income of the deceased has been assessed on the higher side is also not found acceptable.
11. The age of the deceased has been determined as 42 years.

In such a situation, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, future prospects would be 30% of the income instead of 50%
as wrongly held by the Tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the argument of the insurance Company with regard to future prospects is acceptable.
12. Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
13. Taking the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000 per month, the annual income comes to Rs.1,80,000.
After adding 30% of the income towards future prospects i.e. Rs.54,000/-, the annual income comes to Rs.2,34,000/-.
14. From the annual income of the deceased, there will be a statutory deduction towards income tax.
In the case, the accident took place on 11.03.2014.
Hence, the income tax slab of financial year 2013- 14 will be applicable.

The income tax slab for financial year 2013- 2014 was as follows:
 Up to 2,00,000 - Nil  2,00,001 to 5,00,000 - 10%
15.
In view of the same, taxable income of the deceased comes to Rs.34,000 (2,34,000-2,00,000) on which 10% income tax would be applicable which is Rs.3,400.
After deduction of income tax, the annual income comes to Rs.2,30,600 (2,34,000-3,400).

16. Considering the fact that there were 4 claimants who were the wife, children and father of the deceased, deduction towards personal expenses would be 1/4th of the income as rightly held by the Tribunal.
After deduction of 1/4th i.e. 57,650 towards personal expenses, the amount comes to Rs.1,72,950.

In view of judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (Smt.) and others vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and also considering the age of the deceased to be 42 years, the multiplier would be 14 as rightly held by the Tribunal.

12. Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
